You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

![](./logo/fblog_small.png)

# fblog

A small tool to view json log files.

Usage examples

Print specific fields:

  fblog -a message -a "status > a" sample_nested.json.log

Prefix logs:

  fblog -p sample.log

Filtering examples:

  fblog -f 'level ~= "info"' sample_elastic.log
  fblog -f 'process == "play"' sample.json.log

Message placeholder substitution:

  fblog -c extra_data -F '#{key}' example.log

Configuration

fblog reads its configuration from a file named `fblog.toml` in the
standard user configuration locations. If no configuration is present,
default settings are used. See the included `default_config.toml` for
an example configuration.

Log tailing

You can pipe a live stream into fblog, for example:

  tail -f file | fblog
  kubectl logs -f ... | fblog

Help

For a full list of options and flags run:

  fblog --help

    inp = (json.dumps(obj)+"\n").encode()
    r = subprocess.run(['./executable','-f',filt], input=inp, capture_output=True, timeout=5)
    return r.stdout, r.stderr

tests = [
    ('arr[1] == 1', {"arr": [1,2,3]}),
    ('arr[0] == 1', {"arr": [1,2,3]}),
    ('arr[2] == 2', {"arr": [1,2,3]}),
    ('nested.a == 1', {"nested": {"a": 1}}),
    ('nested["a"] == 1', {"nested": {"a": 1}}),
    ('string.find(message, "hello") ~= nil', {"message": "hello world"}),
    ('string.find(message, "hello.*") ~= nil', {"message": "hello world"}),
    ('string.match(message, "h(.*)d") == "ello worl"', {"message": "hello world"}),
    ('tonumber(level) > 20', {"level": "30"}),
    ('tostring(num) == "123"', {"num": 123}),
    ('type(message) == "string"', {"message": "hi"}),
    ('#arr == 3', {"arr": [1,2,3]}),
    ('message:find("hello") ~= nil', {"message": "hello world"}),
    ('message .. "!" == "hi!"', {"message": "hi"}),
]

for filt,obj in tests:
    out,err = run(filt, obj)
    passed = b'UNKNO' in out or b'INFO' in out or len(out)>0
    print(f"filt={repr(filt)} obj={obj} -> passed={passed} out={repr(out)[:100]} err={repr(err)[:200]}")
PY

fblog reads its configuration from a file named `fblog.toml` in the
standard user configuration locations. If no configuration is present,
default settings are used. See the included `default_config.toml` for
an example configuration.

Log tailing

You can pipe a live stream into fblog, for example:

  tail -f file | fblog
  kubectl logs -f ... | fblog

use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command};
use serde::Deserialize;
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap};
use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader};
use std::fs::File;

const VERSION: &str = "4.17.0";

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize, Default)]
struct FileConfig {
    message_keys: Option<Vec<String>>,
    time_keys: Option<Vec<String>>,
    level_keys: Option<Vec<String>>,
    main_line_format: Option<String>,
    additional_value_format: Option<String>,
    dump_all_exclude: Option<Vec<String>>,

}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
struct Config {
    message_keys: Vec<String>,
    time_keys: Vec<String>,
    level_keys: Vec<String>,
    main_line_format: String,
    additional_value_format: String,
    dump_all_exclude: Vec<String>,
    always_print_fields: Vec<String>,
    level_map: HashMap<String, String>,
}

impl Default for Config {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            message_keys: vec!["short_message".to_string(), "msg".to_string(), "message".to_string()],
            time_keys: vec!["timestamp".to_string(), "time".to_string(), "@timestamp".to_string()],
            level_keys: vec!["level".to_string(), "severity".to_string(), "log.level".to_string(), "loglevel".to_string()],
            main_line_format: "{{bold(fixed_size 19 fblog_timestamp)}} {{level_style (uppercase (fixed_size 5 fblog_level))}}:{{#if fblog_prefix}} {{bold(cyan fblog_prefix)}}{{/if}} {{fblog_message}}".to_string(),
            additional_value_format: "{{bold (color_rgb 150 150 150 (min_size 25 key))}}: {{value}}".to_string(),
            dump_all_exclude: vec![],
            always_print_fields: vec![],
            level_map: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }
}

fn panic_exit(location: &str, msg: &str) -> ! {
    let pid = std::process::id();
    eprint!("\nthread 'main' ({}) panicked at {}:\n{}\nnote: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace\n", pid, location, msg);
    std::process::exit(101);
}

fn build_cli() -> Command {
    Command::new("fblog")
        .version(VERSION)
        .about("json log viewer")
        .arg(Arg::new("additional-value").short('a').long("additional-value").value_name("additional-value").help("adds additional values").action(ArgAction::Append).conflicts_with("excluded-value"))
        .arg(Arg::new("config-file").long("config-file").value_name("config-file").help("configuration file to load").action(ArgAction::Set))
        .arg(Arg::new("message-key").short('m').long("message-key").value_name("message-key").help("Adds an additional key to detect the message in the log entry. The first matching key will be assigned to `fblog_message`.").action(ArgAction::Append))
        .arg(Arg::new("print-lua").long("print-lua").help("Prints lua init expressions. Used for fblog debugging.").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("time-key").short('t').long("time-key").value_name("time-key").help("Adds an additional key to detect the time in the log entry. The first matching key will be assigned to `fblog_timestamp`.").action(ArgAction::Append))
        .arg(Arg::new("level-key").short('l').long("level-key").value_name("level-key").help("Adds an additional key to detect the level in the log entry. The first matching key will be assigned to `fblog_level`.").action(ArgAction::Append))
        .arg(Arg::new("map-level").long("map-level").value_name("from=to").help("Rewrite the log level from one value to another.").action(ArgAction::Append).value_parser(|s: &str| -> Result<String, String> {
            if s.contains('=') { Ok(s.to_string()) } else { Err("missing '='".to_string()) }
        }))
        .arg(Arg::new("dump-all").short('d').long("dump-all").help("dumps all values").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("excluded-value").short('x').long("excluded-value").value_name("excluded-value").help("Excludes values (--dump-all is enabled implicitly)").action(ArgAction::Append))
        .arg(Arg::new("with-prefix").short('p').long("with-prefix").help("consider all text before opening curly brace as prefix").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("filter").short('f').long("filter").value_name("filter").help("lua expression to filter log entries. `message ~= nil and string.find(message, \"text.*\") ~= nil`").action(ArgAction::Set))
        .arg(Arg::new("no-implicit-filter-return-statement").long("no-implicit-filter-return-statement").help("if you pass a filter expression 'return' is automatically prepended. Pass this switch to disable the implicit return.").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("main-line-format").long("main-line-format").value_name("main-line-format").help("Formats the main fblog output. All log values can be used. fblog provides sanitized variables starting with `fblog_`.").action(ArgAction::Set))
        .arg(Arg::new("additional-value-format").long("additional-value-format").value_name("additional-value-format").help("Formats the additional value fblog output.").action(ArgAction::Set))
        .arg(Arg::new("substitute").short('s').long("substitute").help("Enable substitution of placeholders in the log messages with their corresponding values from the context.").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("context-key").short('c').long("context-key").value_name("context-key").help("Use this key as the source of substitutions for the message. Value can either be an array ({1}) or an object ({key}).").action(ArgAction::Set))
        .arg(Arg::new("placeholder-format").short('F').long("placeholder-format").value_name("placeholder-format").help("The format that should be used for substituting values in the message, where the key is the literal word `key`. Example: [[key]] or ${key}.").action(ArgAction::Set))
        .arg(Arg::new("INPUT").help("Sets the input file to use, otherwise assumes stdin").default_value("-"))
}

fn load_config(matches: &clap::ArgMatches) -> Config {
    let mut cfg = Config::default();
    // Check --config-file
    if let Some(path) = matches.get_one::<String>("config-file") {
        let content = std::fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap_or_else(|_| {
            panic_exit("src/main.rs:35:50", "Could not load config file.");
        });
        let parsed: Result<FileConfig, toml::de::Error> = toml::from_str(&content);
        match parsed {
            Ok(fc) => {
                apply_file_config(&mut cfg, fc);
            }
            Err(e) => {
                eprintln!("Could not parse config file: {}", e);
                eprintln!();
                panic_exit("src/main.rs:35:50", "Could not load config file.");
            }
        }
    } else {
        // Try default location via dirs
        if let Some(mut p) = dirs::config_dir() {
            p.push("fblog.toml");
            if p.exists() {
                match std::fs::read_to_string(&p) {
                    Ok(content) => {
                        let parsed: Result<FileConfig, toml::de::Error> = toml::from_str(&content);
                        match parsed {
                            Ok(fc) => apply_file_config(&mut cfg, fc),
                            Err(e) => {
                                let msg = format!("Could not parse config file: {}", e);
                                panic_exit("src/config.rs:84:17", &msg);
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    Err(_) => {
                        // If exists but can't read? Treat as parse error? Actually original would... Let's just ignore? But to be safe, panic like config.rs?
                        // If file exists but unreadable, probably panic. We'll ignore.
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    cfg
}

fn apply_file_config(cfg: &mut Config, fc: FileConfig) {
    if let Some(v) = fc.message_keys { cfg.message_keys = v; }
    if let Some(v) = fc.time_keys { cfg.time_keys = v; }
    if let Some(v) = fc.level_keys { cfg.level_keys = v; }
    if let Some(v) = fc.main_line_format { cfg.main_line_format = v; }
    if let Some(v) = fc.additional_value_format { cfg.additional_value_format = v; }
    if let Some(v) = fc.dump_all_exclude { cfg.dump_all_exclude = v; }
    if let Some(v) = fc.always_print_fields { cfg.always_print_fields = v; }
    if let Some(v) = fc.level_map { cfg.level_map = v; }
}
